title.rendered: If You Abide in Me: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: If you abide in Me, and My words abide in you, you will ask what you desire, and it shall be done for you. Two conditions. One extraordinary promise. Abiding is the door through which everything else in prayer walks.

content.rendered:
If you abide in Me, and My words abide in you, you will ask what you desire, and it shall be done for you. Two conditions. One extraordinary promise. Abiding is the door through which everything else in prayer walks.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, July 28, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“If you abide in Me, and My words abide in you, you will ask what you desire, and it shall be done for you.”
John 15:7 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

John 15 records Jesus’ final teaching to His disciples on the night before the cross. He gathers them around the image of the vine and the branches. The branch has no life of its own. It bears fruit only as it remains connected to the vine. Everything about Christian life, service, and answered prayer flows out of that connection. And in verse 7, Jesus tells them what the connected branch can expect from the Father. Ask what you desire. It will be done.

The Passion Translation opens up the depth of Jesus’ promise: “But if you live in life-union with me and if my words live powerfully within you, then you can ask whatever you desire and it will be done” (John 15:7 TPT). Life-union. That is what abiding actually is. Not a distant relationship. Not a Sunday-morning connection. A continuous, breathing, moment-by-moment sharing of life between the believer and the risen Christ. Out of that life-union, prayer flows differently.

The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds another layer: “If you live in Me [abide vitally united to Me] and My words remain in you and continue to live in your hearts, ask whatever you will, and it shall be done for you” (John 15:7 AMPC). Vitally united. His words continuing to live in the heart. The promise is not a formula. It is the natural outflow of a believer whose life is so shaped by the Word of Christ that what they ask flows from the heart of Christ Himself.

This is why abiding is the door. When the believer is abiding, their desires are being shaped by the indwelling Christ. What they ask for begins to align with what heaven has already decided. The prayer of a branch that is deeply connected to the vine is not the prayer of a self-centred wish list. It is the prayer of Jesus praying through the believer. And the Father delights to answer the prayers of His own Son.

For Gospelbuzz readers walking into a season of standing in the believer’s authority, John 15:7 is the key that unlocks the promise. The way to see answered prayer is not to work harder at prayer technique. It is to abide. Read His Word. Let it live in you. Talk with Him throughout the day. Stay connected. Out of that life-union, whatever you desire will begin to look like what heaven has already promised. And it shall be done.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I abide in Christ and His Word abides in me. Out of that life-union with Him, my desires are being shaped by heaven itself. I am not praying my own selfish wish list. I am praying what the indwelling Christ prays through me. Whatever I ask in that place is being asked in agreement with You. And You have promised it shall be done. I walk today in the abiding, in the Word, in the life-union with Jesus that unlocks every prayer promise You have made. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I abide in Christ. His Word abides in me. Whatever I ask out of that life-union with Him shall be done. The prayer of the abiding branch bears fruit.

Go Deeper in the Word

  • John 14:13-14 (NKJV): Whatever you ask in My name, that I will do
  • 1 John 5:14-15 (NKJV): If we ask anything according to His will, He hears us
